chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Kurdawayh, who said:

I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a well into which rainwater enters, while in it are urine, feces, the urine of beasts, their dung, and the droppings of dogs. He said: “Thirty buckets are to be drawn from it, even if it is foul-smelling.”

key_terms.أَبْوَالُ الدَّوَابِّ: the urine of riding or pack animals
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine as a source of impurity
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well used as a water source
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: it should be drained by drawing water out

ai.seo_question: How should a well be purified if it is contaminated with urine, feces, and animal droppings?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a well contaminated by various impurities, including urine and feces. Imam Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام states that thirty buckets should be drawn from it, even if the well has a foul odor, indicating a prescribed method of purification in this case.
